scope: SOURCE REVIEW IDENTITY ONLY. This pins which extract bytes the web packager may admit for ordinary-road access. It is not a rights review, not an owner approval of any dataset composition, and not a publication approval. A matching hash proves which file was reviewed, nothing more.

sourceInput.job: Trail Mapper normalized ordinary endpoint access roads
sourceInput.generatedAtMeaning: When the native extractor ran. It is not when TIGER or OpenStreetMap last changed any way.
layerOrder: osm-service (OpenStreetMap highway=service, in the order the Overpass response listed the ways)

filters.osmExclusions: Ways marked access=no or access=private without a bicycle allowance, bicycle=no or bicycle=private, or service=drive-through or emergency_access; ways with fewer than two points.

sourceInput.extractor: tools/fetch-tigerweb-access-roads.ps1 in the native repository (git blob 3d5e9a35144e2110eb1b047b91371372e68c6620 at this review)
sourceInput.perWayTimestamps: UNKNOWN. The extract carries no per-way source timestamps or OpenStreetMap way versions; only the extractor's run time above. Historical per-way change dates cannot be recovered from this file and are not stated here.

expectedTransform.derivedFrom: tools/lib/access-package.mjs buildAccessParts applied to the SHA-verified source input above (deterministic: same input bytes, same output bytes)
expectedTransform.scope: Pins the normalized base roads and the tile index. The index lists every service-road tile by SHA-256, so it pins every service road's identity, geometry and extract order. This is a source-review digest of a deterministic transform; it is not an approval. If the normalization algorithm is changed on purpose these digests must be re-derived and re-reviewed.

nativeBaseline.statement: This is the access extract the native app ships. The architect independently matched the same SHA-256 to the built-local APK asset on 2026-10-02 (3424 TIGER roads, 9313 OpenStreetMap service roads).
nativeBaseline.nativeDocumentation: docs/routing-data-plan.md (native repository) records the 2026-09-27 refresh that produced it.

futureSources: A re-run extractor, a refreshed extract, or any file with a different SHA-256 is a different source. It needs a fresh entry here, with its own review identity, before the packager will admit it. Editing this hash to match a new file without that review defeats the pin and is a review failure.

rights.note: TIGER/Line is U.S. Census Bureau public-domain data. OpenStreetMap service roads are ODbL; whether a merged routing graph is a derivative database is unresolved (docs/web/data-rights.md). Nothing in this manifest grants or implies a right to publish.
